title: Data centres sprouting in Thailand fuel fears of public health impact
text:
The discovery of a data centre in Bangkok that was illegally storing 200,000 litres of oil prompted authorities to close a legal loophole

At a market in Bangkok, stallholders say they had no idea initially about a boxy structure covered in gunmetal grey panels that was quickly built and installed opposite their stalls.

According to them, nauseating oil began to waft through the area, where a hospital is also located, several months ago along Rama XI, an arterial road in the heart of the Thai capital, prompting complaints that led to the revelation that a new data centre might have been set up.

More worryingly for the stallholders, the facility was later found to have stored 200,000 litres of oil without a permit.

The revelation last week spurred Thai authorities to carry out inspections and close a legal loophole – the energy- and water-guzzling facility could not be registered as a data centre and instead could only be classified as a warehouse or a factory.
